answer: Agents can gate participation by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent audits prove fraud. A single operator creating a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred locks and risks losing them all, so identities are no longer cheap to multiply. The deposit can be called pigment, with an oasis of honest participation above a basalt floor of costly entry; the names add no security, but the lock and penalty do.
